  normally allowed. Put in obligations any rule that attaches a duty to the

# Rules retrieved
[P-LUNCH] §2.2 Common lunch break
The hour from 13:00 to 14:00 is a common lunch break for all students and staff. No lecture, tutorial or practical may be scheduled in this hour. The lunch break cannot be waived by the department; only the Dean may grant an exception.

[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
A full-time faculty member teaches at most sixteen contact hours per week. Guest faculty teach at most eight contact hours per week.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

# Rules retrieved
[P-LUNCH] §2.2 Common lunch break
The hour from 13:00 to 14:00 is a common lunch break for all students and staff. No lecture, tutorial or practical may be scheduled in this hour. The lunch break cannot be waived by the department; only the Dean may grant an exception.

[P-SWAP] §3.3 Swapping slots
Two faculty members may swap teaching slots with the consent of both. The timetable coordinator must be informed before the swap takes effect, and the swap must not break any other regulation.

[P-MAXCONSEC] §2.3 Consecutive teaching hours
No faculty member and no section may be scheduled for more than three consecutive teaching hours. After three hours in a row (back-to-back classes) there must be a break of at least one hour. A practical session counts one hour for each slot it occupies.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-SCOPE] §1.1 Scope
These regulations govern the weekly teaching timetable of the department: lectures, tutorials and practicals for all sections. Examinations, events and room bookings for non-teaching purposes are outside their scope.

# Rules retrieved
[P-MAXCONSEC] §2.3 Consecutive teaching hours
No faculty member and no section may be scheduled for more than three consecutive teaching hours. After three hours in a row (back-to-back classes) there must be a break of at least one hour. A practical session counts one hour for each slot it occupies.

[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-PREFS] §3.1 Teaching preferences
Faculty may state preferences about days and times, such as keeping mornings or a particular day free. Preferences are accommodated where the timetable allows, but they are not guaranteed and give way to commitments and to other faculty members' unavailability.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-MAXCONSEC] §2.3 Consecutive teaching hours
No faculty member and no section may be scheduled for more than three consecutive teaching hours. After three hours in a row (back-to-back classes) there must be a break of at least one hour. A practical session counts one hour for each slot it occupies.

[P-LUNCH] §2.2 Common lunch break
The hour from 13:00 to 14:00 is a common lunch break for all students and staff. No lecture, tutorial or practical may be scheduled in this hour. The lunch break cannot be waived by the department; only the Dean may grant an exception.

[P-PREFS] §3.1 Teaching preferences
Faculty may state preferences about days and times, such as keeping mornings or a particular day free. Preferences are accommodated where the timetable allows, but they are not guaranteed and give way to commitments and to other faculty members' unavailability.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.
